localChanges: `getPreloadedImage` returned `image.cloneNode()` on every lookup. A clone is detached, so it is neither rendered nor decoded and its `width` reads 0 on first use -- which `replaceColours` fed straight into `getImageData` as a zero-sized rect, throwing `IndexSizeError` the first time a unit image was used (the city build header) (#8). No caller mutated the element, so the clone was also an allocation per lookup on the render hot path.

Return the preloaded element itself and size from `naturalWidth`/ `naturalHeight`, which the `#preload` originals report correctly because the container clips them rather than hiding them. `replaceColours` and `Map.putImage` now bail out on a source with no dimensions instead of throwing, since the preload is asynchronous and an early render can arrive first.
With the clone gone the derived canvases can be cached rather than rebuilt:
`replaceColours` returns its cache entry directly instead of cloning it per hit, and keys on the source colours too -- the same sprite recoloured from a different source set is a different result.
`renderUnit` caches the fully rendered unit, keyed on type, colours, fortified and busy state, and composites the overlays onto its own canvas so it never draws on the shared recolour entry.
`Map/Land` caches the composed coast tile by its 8-neighbour bitmask, which bounds it at 256 small canvases instead of one per coast tile per render.
A cache entry is skipped whenever it would be built from an image that had not decoded, so a missing sprite cannot stick for the session, and all three drop when the preload container changes.

Verified against a real asset import (TER257.PIC/SP257.PIC) with the stress harness: 171 turns, no render errors, no zero-sized `getImageData`, and `getImageData` calls -- one per recolour cache miss -- flat at 6 to 12 across the run rather than one per unit per render.
